text:
jamie: Customer on Python 3.10 says after `pip install -e git+ssh://git.example.com/org/redwood-sdk.git@feature/cli#egg=redwood-sdk` their app does `from redwood import client` and gets ImportError. Installing from PyPI works fine. Any ideas?

sara: Can you confirm the exact pip command and whether they used a constraints file or pinned distro?

jamie: They ran `pip install -e git+ssh://git.example.com/org/redwood-sdk.git@feature/cli#egg=redwood-sdk` in a virtualenv. `python -c "import redwood; print(redwood.__file__)"` prints the repo root path but `from redwood.client import RedwoodClient` -> ImportError: cannot import name 'client'

eng-anna: Likely a package name/layout mismatch. Many repos use src/ layout and the actual package might be named `redwood_sdk`. Editable installs and the `#egg=` fragment can cause distribution name divergences from import name. Any repo tree?

jamie: Customer pasted this snippet: 
```
pyproject.toml
src/
  redwood_sdk/
    __init__.py
    client.py
README.md
```
They expected `from redwood_sdk.client import RedwoodClient` but their app imports `redwood.client`.

devx-chet: If project distribution name is "redwood-sdk" but package dir is `redwood_sdk`, then import should be `import redwood_sdk`. `pip install -e` creates an .egg-link that points to the repo source; if a previously installed distribution named `redwood` exists, it may shadow the repo. Also check `pyproject.toml` project.name and setuptools find config.

jamie: Repro suggestions for us: clone the branch and run `pip install -e .` then `python -c "import redwood; print(dir(redwood))"` to reproduce. Also try `pip install git+https://...@feature/cli` (non-editable) to see if wheel metadata normalizes names.

sara: Additional clue: customer has a constraints file at monorepo root pinning `redwood==1.2.0`. pip printed "Requirement already satisfied: redwood==1.2.0 in /usr/local/lib/..." and skipped linking editable.

eng-anna: That explains it. If a pinned distribution is already present, editable install won't overlay it. Recommend uninstalling the pinned distro and any egg-info/dist-info before installing editable. Steps to share: 
1) `pip uninstall redwood redwood-sdk`
2) delete any `redwood*.egg-info` or `redwood*.dist-info` from site-packages if they remain
3) `pip install -e .` (or `pip install -e .[cli]` if extras needed)

jamie: Customer said they ran `pip uninstall redwood` but still got the ImportError; they later discovered a leftover `redwood.egg-info` created by a previous build.

devx-chet: Also suggest verifying package discovery config in pyproject. Example snippet to check: 
```
[project]
name = "redwood-sdk"  # distribution name

[tool.setuptools.packages.find]
where = ["src"]
include = ["redwood_sdk*"]
```
If they meant to `import redwood` they'd need a top-level package named `redwood` (or add a shim module). Alternatively update docs to use `redwood_sdk` import path.

jamie: I'll send repro steps and the egg-info cleanup steps to the customer, and recommend `pip install -e . --no-deps` if constraints cause issues. I'll also file a doc request to clarify recommended `#egg=` usage and repo layout for editable installs.

support-bot: Escalation created: support/priority-high. @eng-anna assigned for follow-up if still blocked.

jamie: thanks all :thumbsup:
